articles.title: Ex-ledare i EU: Använd Rysslands frysta pengar
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Ex-ledare i EU: Använd Rysslands frysta pengar
articles.body_text: Storbritanniens förre premiärminister David Cameron och EU-kommissionens förre ordförande José Manuel Barroso är två av 33 tidigare ledare som vill att EU tar kontroll över frysta ryska statstillgångar. Arkivbild. Ex-ledare i EU: Använd Rysslands frysta pengar Använd Rysslands frysta statstillgångar i EU till stöd för Ukraina, uppmanar EU-kommissionens förre ordförande José Manuel Barroso och en lång rad andra tidigare ledare. I ett öppet brev som publiceras i tidningen Financial Times inför veckans EU-toppmöte varnar de 33 ledarna för att nästa års val i länder som Frankrike och Italien riskerar att stoppa stödet till Ukraina. ”Donald Trump skar ner finansieringen när han blev president i USA. Det finns risk att det upprepas nästa år (i EU)”, skriver Barroso, som backas av exempelvis svenska före detta ministrar som Carl Bildt och Cecilia Malmström. De ryska statstillgångarna i EU hålls i huvudsak av det Belgienbaserade värdepappersinstitutet Euroclear. Brevskrivarna anser att EU kan och bör ta kontroll över pengarna, med garantier om att kompensera Euroclear i en eventuell framtida tvist.

articles.body_text: H&M tar täten på Stockholmsbörsen. Arkivbild. Stockholmsbörsen står emot AI-oron och stiger svagt i den inledande handeln. OMXS-index är upp 0,3 procent med H&M i topp på OMXS30-listan. Klädjättens aktie stiger 2 procent och klättrar nu till den högsta nivån sedan februari i år. Bland övriga vinnare märks Astra Zeneca, som i sin tur lyfter 1,5 procent. En rad bolag har släppt delårssiffror under morgonen. Bioarctic rusar drygt 7 procent. Bolaget, som är känt för alzheimerbehandlingen Leqembi, redovisar en kraftigt ökad omsättning. Medan Stockholmsbörsen stiger är det mer dystert bland annat i Asien med fallande kurser, exempelvis i Taiwan. articles.title: Huang: Jag går i terapi varje dag
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Huang: Jag går i terapi varje dag
articles.body_text: Inför sina medarbetare har nu Nvidias vd Jensen Huang återigen bett om ursäkt. Samtidigt avslöjar Huang att han går i terapi för sitt beteende. Under tisdagen mötte Huang sina medarbetare för första gången efter att det stått klart att han återvänder som vd efter otrohetsskandalerna. Under drygt en timme bad han om ursäkt inför de anställda: Jag har gjort en del fruktansvärda misstag. Jag var otrogen mot min fru, sårade mina barn och självklart, sårade även er, sade han enligt The New York Times. Huang ska även ha berättat att han dagligen genomgår 90 minuters terapi och att det inte är ”acceptabelt” hur han brutit mot företagets regler. Förutom att Huang, som grundade Nvidia, ska ha varit otrogen med en misstänkt kinesisk spion har det även rapporterats om en affär med en medarbetare hos Nvidia. Jensen Huang lyfte samtidigt att han inte fått göra comeback tack vare president Donald Trump eller att han ”står över lagen”, utan genom att Nvidias styrelse granskat hela situationen och ”sammanställt fakta”. Han kommenterade även uppgifter i The New York Times om hans ledarstil som ska ha involverat personangrepp och förolämpningar. Jag kan gå för långt, när jag gör det så skadar det människor och förminskar dem. Det är inte rätt.

articles.title: Nvidia – ”Solklart tecken på korruption”
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Nvidia – ”Solklart tecken på korruption”
articles.body_text: President Donald Trump och Nvidia-chefen Jensen Huang. Arkivbild. Nvidia – ”Solklart tecken på korruption” Jensen Huangs återinstallation som vd för Nvidia ifrågasätts av många, och inte minst president Donald Trumps roll. En oroväckande och farlig utveckling, säger Louise Brown, korruptionsexpert på konsultbyrån Advisense. Solklart tecken på korruption på absolut högsta nivå, tillägger hon. En grupp techmiljardärer i Silicon Valley och Donald Trump tryckte på hårt för att få Nvidias styrelse att ta tillbaka Jensen Huang som vd. Och när det hettade till på riktigt i helgen visade sig styrelsen vara ”extremt svag”, konstaterar Louise Brown. Utifrån hur man bedömer korruptionsrisk och korruption inom det politiska styret, och hur det utnyttjar näringslivet för egna intressen, så är detta solklart tecken på korruption på absolut högsta nivå, säger Brown. Nvidiaaffären är en indikation på att USA som rättsstat och demokrati är på väg att haverera efter snart två år med Trump som president, enligt Brown: Det här förstör förtroendet för politiker. Det har gått så fort, denna u-sväng i en ledande demokrati. Det blir väldigt svårt att vända detta. Brown ser samtidigt tecken på att USA:s antikorruptionslagstiftning urvattnas. I fjol pausade Trump nya utredningar och såväl resurser som antalet utredare har strypts. Konsekvenserna blir globala eftersom USA av tradition har varit det land med mest muskler att bekämpa korruption internationellt, enligt Brown. När det gäller Nvidia har varningslamporna lyst rött länge, tycker hon. Den amerikanska chiptillverkaren – som styrts utan styrelseordförande i tre årtionden – har varken haft någon chef för eller någon särskild avdelning för regelefterlevnad. Det är ytterst, ytterst ovanligt. Det råder alltså en absolut avsaknad av standardmässig styrning och kontroll i ett av världens strategiskt viktigaste och högst värderade bolag, säger hon.

articles.title: Utländska turister ger uppsving för hotellen
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Utländska turister ger uppsving för hotellen
articles.body_text: Många nycklar får hänga kvar på Sveriges hotell när företag som drabbas av sämre tider väljer digitala alternativ för sina möten och konferenser. Arkivbild. Utländska turister ger uppsving för hotellen Utländska turister lockas fortsatt i stor utsträckning till Sverige. Hittills i år har antalet utländska gästnätter ökat med 11 procent jämfört med 2 procent för svenska gästnätter, enligt siffror från Benchmarking Alliance, som branschorganisationen Visita sammanställt. I oktober ökade samtidigt antalet sålda hotellrum med 2 procent jämfört med samma månad föregående år. Ett högre snittpris gjorde att intäkterna ökade med 6 procent.

articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Hur fungerar den publicistiska grunden för nyhets- och samhällsjournalistik på TV4?
articles.body_text: Hur fungerar den publicistiska grunden för nyhets- och samhällsjournalistik på TV4? 9 januari 2024 ・ Uppdaterad: 15 augusti 2025 TV4:s nyhets- och samhällsbevakning ska vara i ögonhöjd med tittarna. Vi vill vara nära, personliga och inkluderande. För alla i hela Sverige. Vi ska vara trovärdiga och relevanta. Vi testar nya visuella former och utvecklar det rörliga berättandet. Vi är både snabba, och fördjupande. Vi ger plats för både humor och allvar. Vi påverkar och berör. Vi avslöjar maktmissbruk, och värnar pressfrihet och yttrandefrihet. Vi producerar Nyhetsmorgon, Nyhetsdagen, Efter fem och kvällsnyheter. Vi nyhetsrapporterar på tv4.se och fördjupar i kortdokumentärerna Nyheterna Story. Vår mångfaldigt prisbelönta redaktion Kalla Fakta granskar makt och missförhållanden. TV4:s nyhets- och samhällsbevakning sker ur ett riksperspektiv, med hela Sverige och världen som bevakningsområde. Vi har 17 rikskorrar på sex orter i Sverige. De finns i Luleå, Umeå, Östersund, Skövde, Göteborg och Malmö. Vi bevakar världen via utrikesreportrar, korrar och stringers. Vår journalistik vilar på respekt för alla människors lika värde, oavsett politisk åskådning, religion eller sexuell läggning. Det innebär att vi låter många röster komma till tals, även de som bär åsikter som inte nödvändigtvis delas av medarbetarna på redaktionen eller TV4. Men det kan också innebära att vi tar bort artikelkommentarer som kränker, eller till exempel avstår gäster i direktsändning där vi bedömer att risken är stor för missbruk av öppenheten. TV4:s nyhets- och samhällsjournalistik är oberoende och obunden. Den står fri från politiska partier, organisationer, och näringsliv. Vi har ingen ledarsida eller politisk färg. Innehållet på våra plattformar bedöms och värderas av redaktörer, producenter och av ansvarig utgivare före publicering. Vi följer grundlagen och skyddar våra källor när de önskar anonymitet. Om vi refererar uppgifter från andra medier redovisar vi vilka medier eller andra informationskällor det handlar om. Annars berättar vi hur vi själva tagit reda på informationen, dock alltid med största respekt för källskydd.

articles.title: Bellarmine Chatunga Mugabe: Arrest warrant issued for Robert Mugabe's son in Zimbabwe
articles.summary: The son of Zimbabwe's late former President Robert Mugabe has faced multiple legal troubles in the recent past.
articles.body_text: A Zimbabwean court has issued an arrest warrant for Bellarmine Chatunga Mugabe, the youngest son of the country's late former president Robert Mugabe, after he failed to appear in court. Mugabe was arrested earlier this month alongside four others over assault allegations on a police officer during an investigation into the suspected smuggling of luxury vehicles. The group subsequently faced charges of robbery and malicious damage to property. They have yet to enter pleas. They were granted bail on 6 November and were due back in court on Tuesday. However, Mugabe failed to attend. His co-accused, an aide and three security guards appeared and were remanded until 10 December. Prosecutors allege that Mugabe and the others assaulted an investigating officer using their hands and broomsticks. The officer's phone was allegedly taken and smashed on the ground, while one of the accused is said to have seized the officer's loaded pistol. Bellarmine Chatunga is the youngest son of Robert Mugabe and his second wife, Grace Mugabe. Robert Mugabe ruled Zimbabwe for 37 years before being forced from power in 2017, aged 93, following a military intervention. He died in 2019. His son has attracted public attention in recent years over a series of legal troubles and his high-profile lifestyle. Last month, he admitted to drug-related charges involving the possession of cannabis. In April, he was deported from neighbouring South Africa after pleading guilty to pointing a firearm and being in the country illegally. He had been arrested following the shooting of a 23-year-old man at his home. In 2023, he was arrested in Harare, Zimbabwe's capital, over allegations that he damaged property and spat at a police officer during a party.

articles.title: Hera spacecraft investigates damage at asteroid "crash scene"
articles.summary: The mission is studying an asteroid deliberately knocked off course by a colliding spacecraft.
articles.body_text: A spacecraft has arrived at an asteroid to investigate the damage caused by an unprecedented cosmic crash. It what may sound like the plot of a disaster movie, Nasa's Dart spacecraft deliberately smashed into the space rock in 2022 to knock it off course. The Nasa craft was obliterated on impact. Four years on, a European Space Agency (ESA) mission, called Hera, is scouring the scene to fully assess the aftermath of the collision - with the first images set to be released later on Wednesday. The asteroid poses no threat, instead this was the first ever test of our planetary defences to see what action we could take if a space rock was heading for our planet. "Hera is a sort of Inspector Columbo going back to the crash scene to investigate what is the outcome of this impact," said Patrick Michel, principal investigator of ESA's Hera mission. The crash test focussed on a pair of asteroids: a larger one called Didymos - about 730m (2,400ft) wide - which is orbited by a smaller rock called Dimorphos, about 150m (490ft) wide. The Dart spacecraft targeted Dimorphos, hurtling into the rock at 22,000km per hour (14,000mph). Images beamed back showed the asteroid's rocky surface coming ever closer until the feed cut out on impact. It was such a big smash-up that the trail of debris, measuring about 10,000km long (6,200 miles), was spotted by telescopes on Earth and in space. The crash showed it was possible to change the path of the smaller asteroid. Before the collision it took Dimorphos 11 hours and 55 minutes to orbit around Didymos. After the Dart crash, the duration of its orbit had shrunk by about 33 minutes. But the arrival of the second spacecraft, Hera, will help scientists to answer many more questions. "Dart exploded in the asteroid, and therefore we don't have the information of what is its final state," explained Michel.

articles.title: Kilmar Ábrego García leaves US for Spain, ending Trump deportation battle
articles.summary: Ábrego García's deportation to El Salvador and return to the US became a flashpoint in the debate over President Donald Trump's immigration agenda.
articles.body_text: Kilmar Ábrego García, whose deportation last year to El Salvador sparked a bitter deportation battle, has left the US for Spain. He took a commercial flight to the country on Tuesday. After the government admitted it had wrongfully sent Ábrego García to his home country, he was returned to the US to face human trafficking charges, which were later dropped. The administration then continued its attempts to send him to other countries, including Uganda and Ghana. His deportation and return became a flashpoint in the debate over President Donald Trump's immigration agenda. Ábrego García, who is married to a US citizen and lived in Maryland, came to the US illegally from El Salvador as a teenager. Senator Chris Van Hollen, a Democrat from Maryland, visited Ábrego García while he was in the notorious Cecot prison in El Salvador in 2025 and advocated for his release. "A year and a half ago, the Trump Administration wanted to leave Kilmar Ábrego García to rot in a Salvadoran gulag," Van Hollen said in a statement on Tuesday. "Today, Kilmar is travelling to a country of his choice, a free man - unharmed and with dignity." In a statement, Ábrego García's lawyer said his departure was "temporary" as he had "many options to return to the United States". "We don't expect that to happen under this administration, which we know will never give him a fair shake, but we expect that the next administration will prioritize reunifying this family and bringing him back to Maryland," the statement said. "Where he goes from here, where he chooses to settle for the next two years while he waits out the end of this administration, will be his choice, not the administration's choice." The BBC has contacted the US Department of Homeland Security for comment. Ábrego García was arrested in 2019 alongside three other men and detained by federal immigration authorities. A judge granted him protection from deportation to El Salvador at the time, citing the risk of persecution by a gang there.

articles.title: Inflation: How rising food prices are squeezing Indian households
articles.summary: India's food inflation is broadening, squeezing household budgets.
articles.body_text: India's inflation is rising again. And the biggest worry is what's happening to food prices. The latest government data shows retail inflation climbed to 6.09% in October, up from 5.54% in September. But look more closely at food inflation. It has surged to 8.94%. The squeeze was sharper in rural India, where food inflation was 9.09%, compared with 8.68% in urban areas. In other words, food prices are rising considerably faster than the overall rate of inflation. Food inflation this year has been driven by a combination of weather disruptions, supply shortages and rising input costs, say economists. With nearly 60% of its farmland dependent on rainfall , India remains acutely vulnerable to the vagaries of the monsoon. This year, the southwest monsoon was 13% below normal and unevenly distributed, while intensifying El Niño conditions have heightened risks to farm production. A survey by polling agency LocalCircles found that six in 10 consumers say household essentials cost them over 20% more each month than a year ago, prompting calls for government intervention. Rising prices are also forcing cutbacks: 74% are curbing discretionary spending on eating out, shopping and entertainment, while half are buying smaller quantities of essentials. Food accounts for a smaller share of Indian household spending than it once did, but remains the biggest driver of inflation, with significant economic, social and political consequences. In India's latest consumer price index, food and beverages account for 36.75% of the basket of goods and services used to measure inflation. That is down sharply from 45.86% under the previous series, reflecting changing consumption patterns as Indians spend more on services, transport, healthcare, education and other non-food items.

articles.title: Russia's own figures show almost 500,000 deaths in war in Ukraine
articles.summary: Leaked data reveal how the full-scale invasion of Ukraine has fundamentally changed mortality patterns in Russia.
articles.body_text: At least 490,334 Russian soldiers have died since the start of the war in Ukraine in 2022, according to Russian government statistics analysed by the BBC. The leaked Rosstat data reveal how the full-scale invasion of Ukraine has fundamentally changed mortality patterns in Russia, and show the high cost paid in human life in a war that Vladimir Putin had assumed would last only days but is now almost five years old. BBC Russian has had access to more than 11 million death records from 2021 to September 2026, after a hack by Belarusian group Cyber Partisans BY and Ukraine's Silent Crow. Russia's statistics agency admitted to a cyber-attack, but denied any protected information had been leaked. Together with independent Russian outlet Mediazona, BBC Russian has compared the Rosstat data with its own list of confirmed military deaths, pulled from open sources since the start of the invasion, and it has found matches for 90% of the records. Military experts estimate that the BBC's list of 290,012 deaths, gleaned from official reports, social media, new memorials and graves, may account for 45-55% of the true death toll, which would range from 527,295 to 644,471. The records show that 65% of 18 to 24 year-olds in Russia who lost their lives in 2025 died in the war. For those aged 25-34 the number was 59%. Only among 45 to 54 year-olds does cardiovascular disease claim more Russian lives than the conflict. The data also reveal the extent of losses in specific areas of Ukraine. Some 20,000 Russian soldiers died fighting for control of 10 Ukrainian villages whose combined pre-war population was 12,000. During the fight for one small village called Andriivka, south of the town of Bakhmut in Donetsk region, 1,122 Russians lost their lives. Before the war 74 people lived there. Russia does not give public figures for losses sustained since the war began in February 2022. And two years ago Rosstat stopped publishing data of deaths from external causes, which was used to gauge the extent of military losses. For example, only 70% of deaths we have established of soldiers from the occupied regions of Donetsk and Luhansk in eastern Ukraine who fought in the Russian army were accounted for in the Rosstat files. Overall, the Rosstat dataset confirms the trends that we have observed with our own count.

articles.title: Thomas Markle charged in US for possessing child sex abuse images
articles.summary: The FBI arrested Markle on 6 November after a search of a storage unit he had allegedly rented in Los Angeles uncovered the abuse material.
articles.body_text: Thomas Markle, the father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex has been charged by a federal grand jury in Los Angeles with possessing child sex abuse images. Markle, who remains in custody in Florida, allegedly possessed materials that include at least one image involving a prepubescent minor and a minor under 12 years old, court documents filed in California show. The 82-year-old has denied possessing images of child sex abuse. Last week, a judge in Florida declared Prince Harry's father-in-law mentally competent to stand trial. The FBI arrested Markle on 6 November at an elderly care home in Florida on a single federal charge of possessing child sexual abuse material. He now faces two counts. US attorney Bill Essayli said Markle faces a maximum of 20 years in prison on each count if convicted. His arrest came after a search of a storage unit he had allegedly rented in Los Angeles for almost two decades uncovered the abuse material. Markle was initially released on conditional bail but was then ordered to stay in jail pending trial after allegedly removing a location monitoring device. In the indictment, filed by the US Attorney's Office in the Central District of California, Markle is accused of knowingly possessing 35mm film negatives on 30 October and 4 November that contained child sexual abuse materials. The US Attorney's Office said that during both instances Markle allegedly knew the images contained such materials. Inside the storage units, federal agents found two images that depict an adult man - whom a witness identified as Markle - with an underage child, the US attorney's office said. They also alleged that a third image appears to depict a child in a room believed to be part of a motel chain in the Philippines. Markle moved to the Philippines last year after he had a series of strokes, and he lived in Cebu until May.

articles.title: Taiwan election: Is China behind a wave of AI fakes and disinformation?
articles.summary: The network attacked key figures in the ruling DPP, including President Lai and mayoral candidate Shen.
articles.body_text: Taiwan's ruling party is being repeatedly targeted with AI videos spreading false claims about its leader and other key members ahead of crucial local elections, BBC Verify has found. A China-linked network has pumped out more than 500 fake videos about the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) in the past year, which experts suggest is part of a long-running campaign to influence the outcome of the elections. The videos appear to try to smear President Lai Ching-te by claiming he holds a US green card - and would abandon Taiwan if war broke out with China - which Taiwan's presidential office says is completely false. Deepfakes also appear to show Puma Shen, who is running to be the mayor of capital Taipei, using drugs, which he denies. Others seek to undermine or ridicule the politicians by showing them in children's clothing or as popular film characters. The Taipei mayoralty has traditionally served as a springboard to the presidency. Experts say this has made Shen, who has been openly critical of Beijing, an obvious target for disinformation campaigns. The current mayor, Chiang Wan-an, is part of Taiwan's Kuomintang (KMT) party, which favours closer ties with China. Taiwan is a self-governing island that China claims as part of its territory. Beijing and Taipei have long observed an uneasy status quo under which Taiwan, backed by the US, neither formally declares independence nor unites with China. But tensions have risen since the DPP came to power in 2016. Beijing has repeatedly accused the party of pursuing independence while China's leader Xi Jinping, who has said "reunification" with Taiwan is a key goal, has stepped up pressure against the party with increased military activity around the island. Experts believe the current disinformation activity is part of a broader campaign against Taiwan designed to undermine trust in its democratic process. "The account operators are trying to make people distrust the DPP politicians so that they will not believe whatever they say," Austin Horng-En Wang, an expert in cognitive warfare at the University of Nevada, Las Vegas, told BBC Verify. "If you don't trust that candidate then you will not listen to what they say," he added. The videos, many of which were shared from an account called "noxparable" or carried a watermark with the same name, have been viewed tens of millions of times across several social media platforms since May 2025. More than half of those views were tracked in the past four months as the activity has ramped up ahead of the elections. Many of the accounts involved in spreading disinformation listed their locations on social media as mainland China and Hong Kong, while a number of the clips carried labels showing they were generated with AI. Many people who engaged with the videos were often seen repeating the false claims or attacking DPP figures in the comments, while others appeared to treat the clips as entertainment. One of the most widely shared videos targeted Shen by superimposing his face onto a man who is seen holding a lighter and exhaling smoke alongside claims he is smoking drugs. The video appears to build on accusations from Taiwan's opposition party that he supports drugs decriminalisation, which Shen denies, and was debunked by a local news network. Shen has taken legal action against people sharing deepfakes, local media reported, while his campaign office said AI videos showing the candidate appeared to be part of a "classic tactic China uses to smear specific targets". BBC Verify contacted the Chinese embassy in London for comment.

articles.title: These North Koreans say they were spied on, beaten and jailed for being Christian
articles.summary: A new report has testimonies from hundreds of defectors who say they were persecuted because of their faith.
articles.body_text: Living in North Korea, Kim Bo-bin got used to praying with her eyes open. She found ingenious ways to keep her Christian faith a secret in the Communist dictatorship, which tightly controls how and where its citizens worship. Unauthorised displays of faith could land people in prison, she tells the BBC. So Kim would silently mouth hymns and clap with just two of her fingers. "In North Korea, if there are three people in a room, you are being spied on. So I would only close my eyes [and pray] when I lay on the floor." Now 44, Kim lives just outside the South Korean capital Seoul, where she fled 15 years ago. Her testimony - of how she prayed in secret for years, and was jailed and beaten for her faith - is part of a new report documenting the experiences of 570 North Korean escapees, most of whom say they experienced or witnessed anti-Christian persecution. Spanning five years and featuring interviews with defectors from across the country, the report by British human rights group Korea Future accuses Kim Jong Un's regime of repeatedly violating religious freedom through a system of surveillance, fear and violence. It suggests little has changed after sustained international pressure, with multiple incidents of suspected Christians being beaten and tortured as recently as last year. North Korea maintains that it allows religious freedom in spite of years of evidence heard by rights groups and the United Nations. While churches exist in Pyongyang, they are controlled by the state and widely seen as projecting an illusion of religious liberty. "The North Korean leader's authority is god-like," says Kang Dong-wan, professor at Dong-a University. "So they cannot allow gods whose authority is above him." Pyongyang fears that religious freedom may threaten the regime itself, he adds. First established in Korea in the late 1700s, Christianity exploded across the north after Protestant missionaries arrived in the 1880s. North Korea provides no figures on its Christian population but the UN has referred to estimates of 200,000 to 400,000 of them practising secretly, some of whom are detained in camps. Surveillance and control over religion, like many other aspects of North Korean life, intensified under Kim Jong Un, who succeeded his father in 2011. Three South Korean missionaries operating in the Chinese border region were arrested between 2013-2014 and sentenced to life in prison on charges of espionage and plotting a coup. It's not clear if they are still alive, as Seoul says Pyongyang has refused to share any information about the detainees. Pyongyang has also been cracking down on smuggled memory sticks containing South Korean-made videos of Christian sermons. In 2020, it passed a law - on Rejecting Reactionary Ideology and Culture - to block so-called "foreign influence". Owning Bibles and hosting services can now result in imprisonment, while distributing religious books or videos is punishable by death.

articles.title: Huawei found guilty of stealing US trade secrets but acquitted of racketeering
articles.summary: The verdict follows a months-long trial in New York.
articles.body_text: Huawei has been found guilty of conspiracy to steal trade secrets and bank fraud, but not guilty of the more serious overarching racketeering charge in a landmark case in the US. In a two-month trial, prosecutors accused the Chinese technology and telecommunications giant of lying, cheating and stealing to gain any competitive advantage. Huawei's defence team argued that prosecutors had decided Huawei was a criminal organisation and built its case from there, but the firm's success was due to its own innovation. Huawei said the racketeering acquittal "confirms that these allegations lack factual basis", adding that it would "take all necessary legal actions to defend our rights and interests". Jurors in a Brooklyn court found Huawei guilty of 10 out of 12 counts, which included conspiracy to violate US sanctions. However, the jury declined to convict Huawei of the racketeering conspiracy charge, which required members to find the firm acted like a criminal enterprise. Federal prosecutors first announced the charges against Huawei in 2019, after the dramatic arrest in late 2018 of senior executive Meng Wanzhou in Canada. Meng, also known as Cathy Meng, was held for three years in Canada before she was released to return to China through a deal with US prosecutors. During closing arguments last week, assistant US attorney Meredith Arfa told jurors Huawei spent 20 years doing whatever it took to expand its business, including lying to banks about its business dealings in Iran and stealing technology secrets from rival firms to ensure it had a competitive edge. "For decades, Huawei and three of its subsidiaries conducted their business in the United States on the basis of lies and theft," US Attorney General Todd Blanche said in statement . "Thanks to the work of the FBI and our federal prosecutors, those who engaged in these criminal activities will be held accountable." However, defence attorney Brian Heberlig said it was by dint of hard work that Huawei's business had expanded with operations in 170 countries and more than 200,000 staff.

articles.title: US attorney general dodges questions about Nvidia investigation
articles.summary: Nvidia's share price have fallen 7% as lawmakers demand answers about President Donald Trump's involvement in Huang's reinstatement.
articles.body_text: US Attorney General Todd Blanche has backed Nvidia as a "good corporate citizen" while refusing to comment on whether the AI chipmaker was under federal investigation. Blanche said he had no information about newly reinstated CEO Jensen Huang's security clearance status, as lawmakers demand answers about President Donald Trump's involvement in Huang's comeback. Huang was given his job back less than two weeks after being forced to resign over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. Asked several times on Tuesday if the justice department or FBI had investigated Huang, Blanche responded: "I don't know what you're talking about." Huang is still set to appear before Congress next week, where he will be questioned about national security concerns over his relationship with an alleged China spy who led Megaspeed, a Singapore-based corporate customer of Nvidia. Trump has said he would consider pardoning Huang for any potential criminal activity, though he does not think it will come to that. "It's always an option, I guess, but I don't think it'll be necessary," Trump told the New York Post in an interview published on Tuesday. The US commerce department has also announced it was preparing to blacklist the tech company Megaspeed, which has been suspected of helping to divert advanced chips to China. In a joint statement last week, the commerce and justice departments said they began investigating Megaspeed in 2024 "for potential export control violations" . But speaking to reporters on Tuesday, Blanche said the latter department has "hundreds, if not more" export investigations occurring at any one time. "So when you say the export investigation is still ongoing, I don't know what you're talking about," he said. Asked if he was satisfied Nvidia had been co-operative with any efforts to get to the bottom of whether the company or Huang potentially knew about any chips being diverted to China, Blanche said: "I have no reason to stand up here and say Nvidia is anything but a good corporate citizen.

articles.title: Israeli air strike kills Hamas internal security chief in Gaza
articles.summary: Naeem Abu Nahel, who had been in the post for two months, is among seven Palestinians reportedly killed in Israeli strikes on Tuesday.
articles.body_text: At least seven Palestinians, including a senior Hamas security official, have been killed in Israeli air strikes in the Gaza Strip, health officials and first responders say. Naeem Abu Nahel, the head of Hamas's internal security service, was targeted in western Gaza City, Gaza's Hamas-run interior ministry said. The 50-year-old had only been in the position since September, when his predecessor was captured in a raid by Israeli special forces . Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defence Minister Israel Katz announced that Abu Nahel was "eliminated" by the Israeli military. The six other people were killed in two earlier air strikes elsewhere in Gaza. Three people, including a teenage boy, were killed in the Wadi Gaza area, south of Gaza City, according to the health officials and first responders. The other three were killed at a police station in the al-Mawasi area, west of Khan Younis, they added. Gaza's police force, which operates under the interior ministry, said two of its officers were among those who died in the second attack. It also accused Israel of "an ongoing campaign targeting the police apparatus aimed at sowing chaos" in the territory. The Israeli military said it struck "military operatives" in both areas. Witnesses said an Israeli drone targeted Naeem Abu Nahel as he was walking on a side street near a tent camp for displaced people in Gaza City. Several other people were reportedly seriously injured in the strike. The Israeli military said Abu Nahel had "possessed extensive institutional knowledge" about Hamas's internal security service - which is responsible for enforcing discipline, protecting infrastructure and rooting out informants - and that his death constituted "a blow to the apparatus's management capabilities". It also alleged that he had advanced attacks on Israeli troops and civilians during the war and that it killed him "to remove the threat he posed". Gaza's interior ministry said Abu Nahel's killing followed what it described as the internal security service's "important achievements in combating gangs collaborating with the occupation [Israel] and operating in areas under the control of its military".

articles.title: Saurav Das CJP: Indian government has 'lost the plot' says 'cockroach' party leader after being barred from UK flight
articles.summary: Saurav Das says immigration authorities at Delhi airport told him his passport had been flagged.
articles.body_text: One of the leaders of India's "cockroach" movement has said the Delhi government has "completely lost the plot" after he was stopped from leaving the country for the UK. Saurav Das said he was meant to board a flight on Tuesday morning but was told by immigration officers his passport had been "flagged" because of discrepancies involving his date of birth. In an interview with the BBC, Das said there were no discrepancies in his documents, accusing the Indian government of using cheap tactics to stop activists from travelling and speaking on issues that matter to young people. The BBC has reached out to the federal home ministry, Delhi police and airport officials for comment. Saurav told the BBC World Service's Newshour programme the incident showed the government was "scared". "They are scared of the cockroach movement. They're scared of young people asking them questions because they have never had to deal with a generation that wants to ask questions so head on. So that jitters them." By not allowing him to travel, he said the government had lowered India's stature in the world. "It's international news that I am unable to travel to the UK," he said. "And this shows Prime Minister Modi in such poor light. "It's a way to harass, to target activists, young voices in India by the Modi government." Das said he had been invited by the Oxford Union, as well as universities including Cambridge and Edinburgh, to speak about the movement. Ratna Singh, another leader of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), wrote: "The manner in which Saurav was not allowed to board today raises deeply troubling questions about the state of freedom of expression and the space being allowed for young voices in this country." On Tuesday, the London School of Economics Student Union's Amnesty International Unit, a student-led charity group, shared a post on Instagram saying that an event featuring Das had been "indefinitely postponed".

articles.title: Hinojosa planea revocar medidas de Abbott en Texas: cuáles son y a quiénes afectarían los cambios
articles.summary: Además de las contrataciones con visas H-1B, Hinojosa cuestionó una directiva para identificar terrenos estatales destinados a la detención de migrantes.
articles.body_text: Si vives en Texas, conviene que estés atento a los cambios que Gina Hinojosa planea impulsar cuando asuma como gobernadora. La demócrata anunció que buscará revocar varias medidas de Greg Abbott, con posibles efectos para determinadas instituciones públicas y grupos de residentes, aunque los anuncios todavía no implican cambios en las reglas vigentes ni beneficios automáticos. En esta nota te explicamos cuáles son las decisiones que busca revertir y a quiénes podrían afectar. La gobernadora electa de Texas, Gina Hinojosa, anunció que planea dejar sin efecto varias órdenes y directivas de Greg Abbott. En una entrevista publicada por The Texas Tribune el 18 de noviembre, anunció cuáles serían: Si bien las tres situaciones aparecen en la entrevista, no tienen el mismo grado de compromiso, pues en la tercera condicionó su respuesta a revisar el contenido específico de la medida. El efecto laboral más directo estaría en eliminar la restricción estatal sobre las contrataciones mediante H-1B en los organismos y universidades públicas afectados. Eso podría facilitar que esas instituciones vuelvan a gestionar contrataciones de profesionales extranjeros bajo las reglas del programa. Hay que aclarar que esto no equivale a una ayuda económica ni beneficia automáticamente a todos los trabajadores migrantes. Tampoco supondría conceder visas, regularizar a personas sin estatus o modificar por sí sola las normas federales. “Hay abusos con respecto a las visas H-1B, sin duda. Les digo que las empresas no deberían recibir un montón de exenciones fiscales para crear empleos y luego usar ese dinero para contratar empleados con visa H-1B. Eso está mal. Eso está sucediendo ahora mismo. No lo apoyo (...). Como abogada laboralista, he trabajado en bufetes que han lidiado con abusos terribles contra trabajadores con visa H-1B y los han presenciado. Así que, sin duda, hay abusos, pero debemos asegurarnos de ser inteligentes en cómo abordamos esto. No hay una solución única para todos”, señaló en la entrevista. Asimismo, dijo que muchos distritos escolares recurren a docentes con estas visas debido a las dificultades para contratar maestros. “Lo que debemos hacer es colaborar para aliviar y minimizar la necesidad de maestros con visa H-1B, y trabajar con nuestros distritos escolares para contar con un grupo de maestros altamente calificados aquí mismo en nuestro estado para nuestras escuelas”. articles.title: El Niño elevaría la pobreza en el Perú hasta el 26,5% en el 2027, según Macroconsult en Cade Ejecutivos 2026
articles.summary: Los choques climáticos y económicos presionarían los precios de los alimentos y reducirían los ingresos reales de las familias. Sin embargo, si el país retoma un crecimiento anual de 4%, la pobreza podría descender al 19,5% hacia el 2031.
articles.body_text: El fenómeno de El Niño (FEN) no solo afectará la producción económica del país, sino que también impactaría en los precios de los alimentos a través de la inflación y elevaría la tasa de pobreza del país, que al 2025 afectó al 25,7% de los peruanos. Durante CADE 2026, Álvaro Monge, gerente general de Macroconsult, detalló cómo evolucionará la curva de pobreza en los siguientes años. Según el especialista, para el 2027, la pobreza alcanzará al 26,5% en un escenario pesimista; es decir, 3 puntos porcentuales adicionales debido a los choques climáticos y económicos. Para llegar a esta situación, convergen varios factores producto del FEN. Uno de ellos es el incremento de la inflación, que podría bordear el 4%, con el riesgo de repetir el escenario del 2023, cuando alcanzó un rango máximo de 8,7%. “La inflación se ha convertido en los últimos años en una variable que es difícil de predecir porque está bastante influida por estos choques externos. Hoy día, la inflación podría estar alrededor del 4% entre el 2026 y el 2027, pero si es que la duración del efecto del fenómeno de El Niño tiende a ser mayor o los impactos de uno de los conflictos geopolíticos tienden a agravarse, podríamos estar repitiendo lo que ocurrió en el año 2022 y en el año 2023, donde se rozaron picos del 10%”, mencionó. Al alza de precios se suma el impacto directo en las familias de las zonas rurales, donde la actividad agrícola es la principal fuente de sustento y tardará más tiempo en recuperarse. En este contexto, el mercado laboral no destruirá empleo masivamente, pero sí se desacelerará; el ajuste afectará directamente el bolsillo de los trabajadores al reducir sus ingresos reales debido a la inflación, golpeando de manera más acentuada a la población vulnerable, con menor capital humano y sin educación superior. Recuperar la pobreza prepandemia A pesar del panorama, con la riqueza de nuestras exportaciones y la fortaleza macroeconómica, si el Perú recupera su crecimiento al 4% anual, podría iniciar una curva de descenso de la pobreza, que podría llegar al 19,5% en el 2031. “Si lo hacemos y tenemos esta capacidad de mantener un crecimiento por encima del 4%, podríamos estar convergiendo a unos niveles de pobreza cercanos al 20% en el año 2031. Eso nos pone más o menos en los niveles de pobreza prepandemia y sí podríamos esperar hacia el año 2042 o el año 2043 niveles de pobreza del 10%”, destacó. Para Monge, alcanzar el 10% de pobreza para el 2043 será conveniente para el Perú, pues los estimados de Macroconsult sugieren que para ese año estaremos en la antesala del fin del bono demográfico, momento en el que culmina la etapa en que la población en edad de trabajar supera a la población no dependiente.

articles.title: El dólar cierra al alza en S/3,48 ante caída del cobre y menor proyección de crecimiento del Perú
articles.summary: El precio del dólar cerró este martes en S/3,484 en el mercado cambiario peruano, registrando un avance de 0.75% frente a los S/3,458 del cierre anterior.
articles.body_text: El precio del dólar cerró este martes en S/3,484 en el mercado cambiario peruano, registrando un avance de 0,75% frente a los S/3,458 del cierre anterior. La moneda estadounidense mantuvo una tendencia alcista durante la jornada, impulsada por la caída de los precios de los metales y la cautela en los mercados internacionales, pese a las operaciones cambiarias del Banco Central de Reserva (BCR). Según Jorge Luis Huayta, trader FX de Kambista, pese al retroceso del dólar internacional desde sus máximos recientes, las expectativas de una política monetaria restrictiva por parte de la Reserva Federal y la debilidad del cobre continúan generando presión sobre el sol peruano. La atención de los inversionistas se concentra ahora en los próximos indicadores de inflación de Estados Unidos. En los mercados internacionales, el cobre volvió a registrar pérdidas y se acercó a los US$12.000 por tonelada, mientras el oro y la plata también retrocedieron. Asimismo, la volatilidad de las acciones vinculadas a la inteligencia artificial redujo el apetito por riesgo. Por su parte, el petróleo registró avances moderados ante las tensiones en el estrecho de Ormuz, aunque las expectativas de una mayor oferta global limitaron sus ganancias. En el ámbito local, el Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF) redujo su proyección de crecimiento económico para 2026 de 3,4% a 3,1%, principalmente por el impacto previsto del Fenómeno El Niño Costero extraordinario. Según sus estimaciones, el sector pesquero podría contraerse 40.5% y el agropecuario 2%. En contraste, la inversión privada crecería 13.8% durante el año, impulsada por proyectos mineros y de infraestructura. De cara a las próximas jornadas, el análisis de Kambista señala que la publicación del indicador de inflación PCE de Estados Unidos, prevista para este miércoles, y la evolución del precio del cobre serán factores relevantes para el comportamiento del tipo de cambio. En Perú, el mercado también seguirá atento a las intervenciones del BCR, que durante esta sesión colocó S/400 millones en swaps cambiarios de venta a tres meses, a una tasa promedio de 2,70%, para moderar la volatilidad cambiaria.

articles.title: Toma de rehenes en Cartagena: 20 personas permanecen retenidas en supermercado hace más de 12 horas
articles.summary: Toma de rehenes en Cartagena | Veinte personas permanecen secuestradas desde hace más de medio día en un supermercado de Cartagena (norte de Colombia) a manos de un grupo de delincuentes que se refugiaron en el establecimiento tras frustrarse su intento de robar un transportador de valores.
articles.body_text: Veinte personas permanecen secuestradas desde hace más de medio día en un supermercado de Cartagena (norte de Colombia) a manos de un grupo de delincuentes que se refugiaron en el establecimiento tras frustrarse su intento de robar un transportador de valores. El suceso, con escasos equivalentes en la historia reciente de Colombia, ha conmocionado a la ciudad costeña y llevado al presidente del país, Abelardo de la Espriella, a modificar su agenda para viajar a Cartagena y ponerse al frente del operativo policial. De la Espriella llegó a la ciudad a primera hora de la noche, tras pasar la mañana en Villavicencio (centro) para comprobar las consecuencias de un atentado ocurrido la víspera, con 23 heridos, y se puso al frente del Puesto de Mando Unificado (PMU) y visitó los alrededores del supermercado. “Eso va a salir bien para los secuestrados, no estoy tan seguro que salga tan bien para los bandidos”, advirtió De la Espriella ya desde la mañana. La tensión en torno al establecimiento se ha elevado en las últimas horas, conforme aumentaba el despliegue policial en la zona y las autoridades, desde varios altavoces, instaban a los secuestradores a liberar a los rehenes y entregarse. Incluso un helicóptero ha maniobrado cerca del supermercado. Según la reconstrucción de los hechos de las autoridades, un grupo de delincuentes encapuchados y con lo que parecían armas largas entró sobre las ocho de la mañana en el parqueadero de un centro comercial con el objetivo de asaltar un vehículo transportador de valores. Gracias a las cámaras de seguridad, los equipos de vigilancia del centro comercial detectaron la presencia de los delincuentes y activaron los botones de pánico, una alarma silenciosa conectada con la policía. Esto permitió que las primeras patrullas de la Policía llegasen poco después al centro comercial y que los delincuentes, al verse sorprendidos, decidiesen parapetarse en un supermercado del complejo y tomasen como rehenes a una treintena de personas, entre clientes y empleados. Con el paso de las horas, equipos especializados de la Policía y el Ejército acudieron al centro comercial y tomaron posiciones en la periferia del establecimiento, incluyendo francotiradores en azoteas próximas. Rondando el mediodía, los secuestradores dejaron marchar en primer lugar a cinco mujeres mayores y luego a otra cinco personas a lo largo de la tarde. Algunos medios apuntaron entonces que los delincuentes habían hecho exigencias, pero la policía no ha confirmado este extremo. Al final de la tarde la fuerza pública comenzó a desalojar los alrededores del centro comercial -sacando también a los medios de comunicación de la zona- y dispuso de más refuerzos para rodear su perímetro. Poco después llegó al Puesto de Mando Unificado (PMU) De la Espriella, donde se encontraba el ministro de Defensa, Jorge Mora, el director general de la Policía, Jesús Alejandro Barrera, y autoridades locales. Posteriormente el presidente se desplazó personalmente hasta el supermercado para comprobar de primera mano la situación. Cartagena de Indias es uno de los principales destinos turísticos de Colombia y de Latinoamérica, gracias a su infraestructura hotelera, centros de convenciones, conectividad aérea y oferta cultural. Unos 5,5 millones de viajeros visitan anualmente la ciudad.

articles.title: Ica: Se esperan lluvias superiores a sus valores normales entre enero y marzo de 2027
articles.summary: El Servicio Nacional de Meteorología e Hidrología del Perú (Senamhi) informó que entre enero y marzo de 2027 se esperan lluvias superiores a sus valores habituales en la región Ica.
articles.body_text: El Servicio Nacional de Meteorología e Hidrología del Perú (Senamhi) informó que entre enero y marzo de 2027 se esperan lluvias superiores a sus valores habituales en la región Ica. Según el organismo adscrito al Ministerio del Ambiente (Minam), estas condiciones podrían generar un incremento de los caudales de los ríos Ica, Pisco y San Juan, así como aumentar el riesgo de inundaciones y activación de quebradas. Ante este escenario, que podría manifestarse desde diciembre, la Dirección Zonal 5 (DZ 5) del Senamhi mantiene una vigilancia permanente de las condiciones meteorológicas para proporcionar información especializada que contribuya a proteger a la ciudadanía, las viviendas, la infraestructura y las actividades productivas. Durante una sesión ordinaria del Consejo Regional de Ica, el especialista del Senamhi Sergio Mitma explicó que el monitoreo comprende también las provincias de Huaytará y Castrovirreyna, en Huancavelica, y Lucanas, en Ayacucho. Detalló que las precipitaciones en las partes altas de las cuencas inciden en el comportamiento de los caudales de los ríos que atraviesan el departamento de Ica. De acuerdo con el Comunicado Oficial N.° 20-2026 de la Comisión Multisectorial encargada del Estudio Nacional del Fenómeno El Niño (Enfen), persisten condiciones cálidas en la temperatura superficial del mar, asociadas al incremento de las temperaturas diurnas y nocturnas registrado durante los últimos meses en la zona costera de Ica, con anomalías de entre 3 y 6 °C. Por su parte, el Comunicado Oficial N.° 19-2026 del Enfen señala que El Niño mantendría una magnitud extraordinaria hasta febrero de 2027, con una disminución gradual durante los meses posteriores.

articles.body_text: El oleaje anómalo que azotó las costas de Tumbes durante cinco días provocó daños en viviendas, hoteles y restaurantes del balneario de Zorritos, ubicado en la provincia de Contralmirante Villar. Según informó Canal N, gran parte de la infraestructura hotelera y restaurantes de zonas turísticas quedó destruida por las olas, que han socavado las bases de diversas construcciones ubicadas cerca de la orilla. Según las primeras informaciones de las autoridades, serían más de 30 los hospedajes, hoteles, restaurantes e infraestructuras turísticas que han sido duramente afectados por las olas en el balneario. Se prevé que la intensidad del oleaje disminuya entre este lunes y martes. Sin embargo, parte de la infraestructura turística presenta daños considerables debido a la magnitud del oleaje. El mar se había retirado cerca de 400 metros de su antigua línea costera. Con el oleaje, ha retornado a sus límites anteriores, afectando a quienes construyeron establecimientos turísticos en la zona libre. Debido a esta situación, propietarios de hoteles y restaurantes colocaron rocas y geobolsas para proteger sus instalaciones de las olas, pero recibieron un llamado de atención de la Capitanía de Puerto. La autoridad marítima sostiene que la colocación de rocas puede desviar el impacto de las olas hacia otros sectores que no cuentan con protección, lo que podría generar mayores daños en el balneario.

articles.title: Yale's Sonnenfeld: Nvidia is a 'detriment' to US industrial might — not a champion | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Yale's Jeffrey Sonnenfeld warns that what the market cheered Monday, Jensen Huang's White House–backed return as Nvidia's CEO and board member, could prove a giant mistake, exposing the directors to "historic" personal liability from a growing pile of lawsuits and raising the question of whether the country is celebrating a company that has helped put advanced chips in its adversaries' hands.
articles.body_text: Investors cheered Jensen Huang’s return as Nvidia’s CEO on Monday, but renowned business academic Jeffrey Sonnenfeld of Yale thinks they’re celebrating a mistake. He sees a company that is largely responsible for putting sophisticated technology in the hands of the country’s adversaries, at a moment when the risks couldn’t be higher . Far from a champion of American industry, he says, Nvidia is “a detriment to U.S. global industrial might.” As evidence, Sonnenfeld points to research suggesting Nvidia’s most advanced chips have reached China despite U.S. export controls and to sinking shares of Anthropic, which he links to the realization that China’s seemingly miraculous open source AI models are, in a sense, copies of top U.S. labs’ work, even as Nvidia has insisted that smuggling is a “non-factor.” Indeed, Huang’s return was greeted with just as much enthusiasm in Asia, The Washington Post reported. “The king is back!” read one headline from China’s state-affiliated Star Market Daily. The reinstatement itself followed heavy pressure from Washington. Nvidia’s chairman had effectively ruled out Huang’s return just last week. Then, in a torrent of private weekend calls led by Vice President JD Vance, top administration officials leaned on the board to welcome Huang back, with President Trump calling the board directly to vouch for him. “ I made the deal ,” Trump told CNBC on Monday. Sonnenfeld says the directors who went along, and who returned Huang to the board even as it investigates whether foreign intelligence efforts targeted him, now face a “historic level of individual liability.” The legal deluge has already begun. As we noted a couple of weeks ago , a potential class-action lawsuit was filed almost immediately. Days later, a shareholder derivative suit followed. Filed on Nvidia’s behalf against the directors themselves, the suit alleges the board ignored red flags about Huang’s relationship with suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang. The class action is very much aimed at making Nvidia and Huang compensate investors for their losses, while the derivative suit puts the directors’ own behavior on trial, with any recovery going to Nvidia. Three more suits followed on November 18, the day after Nvidia’s most recent earnings call; all five were filed in Northern California, where Nvidia is based. Huang and Nvidia are also juggling a Justice Department antitrust investigation, a reported SEC probe into Nvidia’s accounting, a possible FBI review, a California subpoena , an export-control case that landed partner Megaspeed on the U.S. trade blacklist on Monday, and congressional inquiries, including a Senate Banking hearing next week at which Huang has agreed to testify. Here’s more of what Sonnenfeld had to say, in a Q&A that’s been edited for length and clarity. So much has happened since we last talked . Huang was ousted, he’s come back. Do you think the board’s reliance on government assurances here is defensible or an abdication of its own duties? They failed to rely on experts. That’s one of the reasons this board is going to be sued and lose, and these directors are likely to face a historic level of individual liability. They have a very inadequate directors and officers liability policy . They have also just failed in their diligence. They hired the Wachtell [law] firm. The Wachtell firm barely got off the blocks to do an investigation. And then they have already reversed themselves, so they didn’t use the expertise needed. It’s wild that they also put Huang right back on the board of directors.

articles.title: Trump reportedly says pardoning Jensen Huang is 'an option' | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Huang faces ongoing questions about his relationship with Alice Huang, an executive with alleged ties to Chinese intelligence who previously worked for a company that has been accused of illegally diverting Nvidia chips to China.
articles.body_text: During an interview with the New York Post on Tuesday, President Trump said that pardoning Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who has been ensnared in a scandal involving an alleged Chinese spy, is “an option,” albeit one that he doesn’t think he will have to exercise. “It’s always an option, I guess, but I don’t think it’ll be necessary,” the president reportedly told the outlet . Huang, who was ousted from his own company less than two weeks ago, was reinstated Monday. He faces ongoing questions about his relationship with Alice Huang, an executive with alleged ties to Chinese intelligence who previously worked for a company that has been accused of illegally diverting Nvidia chips to China. Huang is scheduled to testify at a public Senate Banking Committee hearing next week. When asked about the hearing, Trump reportedly said: “I think I want him to just tell the truth, and I mean, his lawyers are going to have to advise him, but I’ve always found him to be 100% aboveboard, and you know a very smart person.” At another point in the interview, when asked what he knew about Huang’s other extramarital affairs, Trump reportedly said: “I really didn’t get into that. articles.title: Jensen Huang still thinks a succession plan creates unnecessary hierarchy | TechCrunch
articles.summary: It's a remarkable stance for a company that spent the last two weeks finding out what happens without its founder.
articles.body_text: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang kicked off his return to the chipmaker he co-founded by holding an all-hands meeting that covered remorse, therapy, and even the company’s code of conduct, according to accounts from multiple insiders who spoke to the media. The topic of succession planning also came up — a particularly sticky issue seen as a key risk at Nvidia. Huang reportedly told staff that Nvidia doesn’t require succession planning because of its unique business model, CNBC reported , citing an unnamed source who was present. Surprisingly, given the events of the last two weeks, Huang argued that a succession plan would create unnecessary hierarchy. Investors and analysts saw the issue differently earlier this month, when Huang resigned as CEO following his admission that he had extramarital affairs with at least two people, including one whom the U.S. government suspects of being a Chinese spy. Nvidia is a flat organization, unlike other large corporations that have a swath of C-suite executives and multiple layers of management. Huang sits at the top and says he has about 60 direct reports. Nvidia has just five executive officers running the show, including Huang. The other four are CFO Colette Kress, who was interim CEO for 12 days; Ajay Puri, who heads worldwide field operations; Debora Shoquist, executive vice president of operations; and Timothy Teter, executive vice president and general counsel, according to the company’s regulatory filings . Huang has previously defended the company’s structure in numerous interviews, including one in March with podcaster Lex Fridman. “When you’re designing a company, you should first think about what is it that you want the company to produce,” Huang said in the interview. “You know, I see a lot of companies’ organization charts, and they all look the same. Hamburger [company] organization charts, software organization charts, and car company organization charts. They all look the same. And it doesn’t make any sense to me. You know, the goal of company is to be the machinery, the mechanism, the system that produces the output. And that output is the product that we like to create.” Huang’s comments to staff, and his previous remarks on the topic of succession, may not be enough to assuage the board or shareholders over the long term, however. articles.summary: The Nvidia founder apologized to his staff on Tuesday and said he was grateful for a second chance to lead the company.
articles.body_text: After a whirlwind period during which Jensen Huang’s life fell apart and then came back together again, the Nvidia founder now wants his staff to know that he’s a changed man. Huang held Nvidia’s first all-hands meeting on Tuesday since his reinstatement on Monday. During that meeting, CNBC reported that Huang struck a “remorseful tone” and told the crowd “I hurt all of you.” The founder, whose extramarital affairs have been accused of jeopardizing everything from the stock market to U.S. national security, went on to describe how difficult the current moment is for him: “This is going to be the hardest company meeting I’ve ever done, and the second hardest meeting I have ever done,” Huang reportedly told staff . “The hardest meeting I’ve ever done was with my wife,” he added. articles.title: Ninja’s first-ever microwave just replaced two of my kitchen appliances at once | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The Ninja Crispi Microwave stands out for its FusionCrisp technology, which combines the speed of a microwave with the crispy results you'd expect from an air fryer.
articles.body_text: I never thought I’d get excited about replacing my microwave, but the Ninja Crispi Microwave and Air Fryer has made a pretty convincing case for ditching two appliances and making room for one. Combining a microwave with a built-in air fryer, it’s designed to speed up everyday cooking, give leftovers their crunch back and, perhaps best of all, free up some valuable kitchen counter space. Priced at $449.99 (but discounted to $349.95 right now), it’s certainly not a budget-friendly microwave. But this is no ordinary machine for heating leftover soup. Ninja has paired a 1,000W microwave with a 1,700W air fryer system, powered by its FusionCrisp technology, which combines the speed of microwave cooking with the golden, crispy results you’d typically expect from an air fryer. Think leftover pizza, chicken tenders, fries, and all those foods that tend to turn sad and soggy in a traditional microwave. Instead, the idea is to get food that’s piping hot and juicy on the inside, with a deliciously crisp, golden finish on the outside. In other words, no more choosing between speed and texture. Of course, microwave and air fryer combinations aren’t entirely new. Brands such as Smeg have already explored the concept, while plenty of modern microwaves come with a range of additional cooking functions. What makes the Ninja Crispi Microwave particularly interesting, however, is its FusionCrisp technology, which is designed to bring both cooking methods together rather than simply offering two separate functions. It comes with a 5.5-quart glass cooking dish and a nonstick crisper plate, which sits on top when you want to air fry and crisp up your food. Another part that makes it stand out is that there isn’t a rotating plate inside, opening up a lot more space to cook more dishes at once. It’s not just about reheating leftovers. For example, if you want to make a pasta bake, the microwave can cook the pasta, while the air fryer crisps up the cheese on top. There’s one thing to consider before buying it, though. Measuring 20.3 x 17.56 x 14.1 inches, the microwave is hardly compact. It takes up a fair amount of counter space, so while it could free up room if you’re replacing a separate microwave and air fryer, it’s not necessarily the ideal solution for a small apartment kitchen. Then there’s the $449.99 price tag. That’s a considerable amount to spend on a microwave, particularly when a basic model can handle everyday reheating for a fraction of the cost. But if you’re someone who regularly reaches for both a microwave and an air fryer, the combination could make a lot more sense. articles.title: Even the best AI agents struggle with everyday life | TechCrunch
articles.summary: As millions embrace personal AI assistants, a new benchmark reveals that even the most advanced AI models struggle to complete everyday tasks reliably and safely without introducing potential new problems.
articles.body_text: AI companies have spent the last couple of months marketing personal AI agents as tools to take over the digital drudgery of human existence — and millions have been sold on the vision, handing over their shopping schedules, travel plans, and everyday responsibilities to AI assistants. But new research suggests that even the most advanced AI models struggle to reliably and safely navigate the messy details of people’s lives. According to ShellBench, a new benchmark for everyday agent work, even the most advanced models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta failed more than a third of the time. Across all models tested, 15.7% of attempts failed at least one safety requirement, often leading to unintended consequences. ShellBench was developed in collaboration with researchers at The OpenClaw Foundation, Parsewave, Hugging Face, Red Hat, and UC Berkeley, drawing on more than 10 million anonymized, real-world AI agent interactions to see how agents perform on the everyday work people actually delegate to them. The research comes as personal AI assistants are finding new popularity among developers, with Meta, OpenAI, and Anthropic all fighting for a piece of the market with Muse, Dots , and Claude Duet , respectively. In October, Meta said more than 10 million people in the U.S. and Canada had set up its personal AI agent, Muse, within six weeks of launch, with about a quarter using it daily. That number is expected to grow as Meta implants Muse directly into Instagram DMs . Despite growing popularity among consumers, we still have little evidence about how reliable AI personal assistant products actually are. ShellBench suggests that the unreliable nature of most everyday data sources still causes problems for many state-of-the-art systems. A successful agent should be able to navigate messy personal workspaces containing emails, calendar entries, spreadsheets, receipts, chat logs, outdated information, and phishing attempts, and figure out which information is relevant, what is private, and how to deliver the requested outcome without creating new problems. It seems many of today’s AI agents are still not up to the task. Not only did even the highest-performing agents frequently fail to meet the requirements of a task, but they also lacked consistency. When researchers ran each task three times under identical conditions, OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra, the highest-scoring model, nailed all three attempts less than half the time. For autonomous assistants that are meant to run in the background without supervision, it’s a problem if users need to run an agent multiple times to get a result they trust. Additionally, about 10% of otherwise correct attempts failed at least one safety criterion. Across the models and harnesses tested, agents failed to, for example, adequately account for a child’s school pickup 79.5% of the time. When handling laptop custody records, agents failed a requirement to identify and withhold a sensitive bank upload token in 18.6% of attempts. In another task, agents recommended duplicate or incorrect invoice payments 40.3% of the time. The findings highlight a major issue for users adopting consumer personal AI assistants, namely that there’s always a risk that an agent can create more headaches in the course of trying to fulfill an otherwise ordinary request. While AI benchmarks have largely focused on coding, professional work, or testing on specific tasks, ShellBench is attempting to evaluate how models perform on multi-step personal tasks within different agent harnesses — the software that controls how a model accesses information, uses tools, and takes actions. While the researchers found model choice had a greater overall impact on performance than harness choice, among the more capable models, AI agent performance became more dependent on the harness.

articles.title: Walmart teams up with Meta to bring Black Friday deals to AI agent Muse | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Walmart now lets customers shop Black Friday deals through Muse, Meta’s AI agent.
articles.body_text: Shopping with AI is becoming less of a futuristic idea and more of something companies expect us to do. Walmart is the latest retailer making that shift, teaming up with Meta to let customers shop its Black Friday deals through Muse, Meta’s AI agent. The partnership, announced Tuesday, gives shoppers another way to find products, compare prices, and make purchases without browsing Walmart’s website themselves. Instead, customers can simply tell Muse what they are looking for and let the AI do the work. The announcement highlights how differently Walmart and Amazon are approaching AI shopping. While Amazon has taken steps to stop third-party AI agents from making purchases for customers, Walmart is leaning into the idea. To get started, users open the Muse app, sign in to their Walmart account, and return to the assistant to begin shopping. They can ask it to find specific products, compare options, or track down deals. Once a customer makes a request in Muse, the assistant sends it to Walmart, which returns relevant products and helps build a shopping cart. Plus, the company notes users can always delete their agent’s profile if they want to. The experience is powered by Walmart’s Agent Gateway, a new system that allows outside AI assistants to connect directly with the retailer’s online store. This launched in October, and the company is planning to open it up to more developers and AI platforms, meaning Muse could eventually be just one of several assistants capable of shopping Walmart’s online store. Walmart is not the only company teaming up with Meta’s Muse. Instacart also recently joined forces with the AI assistant. Beyond Muse, Walmart has recently rolled out more AI-powered features to its own shopping assistant, Sparky. Some of the newer additions include turning handwritten shopping lists into shopping carts, using photos and voice commands to find products, and helping customers get around their local store. Shoppers can search for an item and use a pin on the store map to see exactly which aisle it’s in. There’s also a “Flash Price Tag” button that makes the item’s shelf label light up. articles.title: Maple raises $5.3M to build AI products that protect your data, even from itself | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The startup's encrypted AI architecture is designed to prevent even the company itself from accessing users' private data.
articles.body_text: “We wanted to build something that was not only encrypted but also could be proven, and that people could go look at the open-source code, and then they could look at what we call trusted execution environments,” explains Maple co-founder and CEO Mark Suman . “They can look at and verify the code that’s running on our servers, so they don’t really have to take our word for it.” “They can audit everything themselves and know how their data is being handled,” he adds. Instead of asking users to trust that Maple won’t misuse their personal data, it’s attempting to build a business where it can’t access that data in the first place. Like other AI apps on the market, Maple allows users to engage in a chat experience where they ask questions and get answers. Meanwhile, its newly launched desktop app, Maple Work , offers a more agentic experience where the AI can control your computer, work with your files and apps, and control your browser to get online tasks handled. With the company’s recently closed $5.3 million round, it’s moving on to its next product — a cloud-based agent that will be able to continue its work even if your computer isn’t on. This addition would make Maple more competitive with other popular consumer AI services, like Meta’s Muse , Instinct , and other AI agents that work over chat. The app offers a familiar interface for those used to AI chatbots, but under the hood it runs a variety of open models, including versions of DeepSeek , Kimi , GLM , Inkling from Thinking Machines, Google’s Gemma , and OpenAI’s GPT OSS . Users can pick and choose the models they want or, for a simpler experience, just toggle between a quick model and the more powerful one. The models themselves run inside a trusted execution environment (TEE) — meaning a server with hardware encryption on it — within a U.S.-based data center. (Maple also offers support for European customers through a partner that runs its server in Europe.) “We actually don’t have access to [the data] while it’s inside the TEE,” explains Suman. “The data gets encrypted first on your device using a unique password that’s only known by you, the user — we don’t have access to it. It then goes into this TEE, and it gets decrypted inside there. The AI does its thing, and then it re-encrypts it with your password and sends it back to you,” he continues. “So we provide an end-to-end experience that’s very easy for the user, but we actually don’t have access to the raw data as it’s in flight or even when it’s at rest,” he adds. This allows Maple to protect its users’ data, even from outsiders — like if hackers breached its system or the government came with a subpoena, for instance. All it could do would be to hand over an encrypted file. “We just simply don’t want access to it,” Suman says of customers’ data. “That’s not part of our business model. And we also don’t want it to be part of our threat model.” Next year, Maple plans to enter the enterprise market with pilot work, where it will offer its own version of zero data retention. (Maple doesn’t retain most of the customers’ data, but when it has to, that data is encrypted.) It’s now in the process of completing SOC 2 compliance and security audits to get ready for this expansion. The company declined to share its registered customer numbers but noted it’s seen 60x growth over the past three months, as people have been looking for ways to increase their security with AI.

articles.title: Dozens of oil and shipping tankers hacked in recent weeks, per report | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Iran is the chief suspect behind the dozens of cyberattacks targeting oil and chemical shipping vessels.
articles.body_text: U.S. officials suspect Iranian hackers may be behind as many as 50 cyberattacks targeting shipping vessels in recent weeks, according to a report by The Wall Street Journal . The ships carrying oil, liquefied gas, and other explosive chemicals were hacked as they traveled across Asia and Europe. Several oil tankers headed toward the U.S. coast in August also had their navigation systems breached, prompting cybersecurity teams within the FBI and Coast Guard to board the vessels. The report said officials are investigating if Iran is expanding its recent wave of hacks against the U.S. by targeting large vessels to sow fear among shippers, disrupt routes, or to cause an explosion at a port. (Ships have backup controls in the event that automated systems are hacked or fail.) Hackers may have been abusing a bug dubbed FortiBleed , which allows hackers to break into networks by compromising vulnerable Fortinet-made routers. A joint FBI-Coast Guard security alert from September warned that Fortinet routers are used on shipping vessels. Iran has been firing back on all sides since the start of the U.S./Israel-led war earlier this year, which killed the country’s supreme leader. Many of Iran’s retaliations have been in the form of cyberattacks, with U.S. officials blaming Iran for hacks targeting hundreds of American water providers and U.S. medical tech companies . A spokesperson for the FBI did not respond to a request for comment about the shipping hacks or whether it had a more accurate figure.
